claims.text: An active-learning machine-learned potential trained on AIMD data will represent the high-temperature solid and liquid configurations of equimolar CoCrFeNiMn more accurately than traditional EAM models.
Using the active-learning potential will significantly reduce the thermodynamic-integration free-energy mismatch for CoCrFeNiMn.
The proposed scope is equimolar CoCrFeNiMn in solid and liquid states at approximately 0.9–1.1 times its melting temperature.
The EAM reference should be replaced by a moment-tensor or deep-neural-network potential iteratively trained and refined using AIMD configurations.
An active-learning workflow can proceed through repeated training, exploration, candidate selection, and ab initio labeling, including training on crystalline and liquid configurations.
Many-body descriptors capture local atomic environments and longer-range correlations in the alloy.
These descriptors bridge the gap between the configurational phase space represented by an empirical EAM potential and the full ab initio ensemble.
Active learning identifies configurations inadequately represented by the current training set and adds appropriate configurations for further training.
Iterative retraining makes the machine-learned energy landscape closely match full DFT calculations over the relevant configuration space.
Closer agreement between the machine-learned and DFT energy landscapes increases reference–target phase-space overlap and reduces mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
Standard EAM references exhibit a typical thermodynamic-integration mismatch of approximately 15%.
Sufficiently trained active-learning potentials can reduce the thermodynamic-integration error below 5%.
TOR-TILD's traditional EAM references have a higher free-energy path mismatch because they represent a limited range of configurations.
The method is expected to apply primarily to near-melting, equimolar CoCrFeNiMn, while transfer to strongly non-equimolar compositions or temperatures far from melting is unvalidated.
The magnitude of improvement depends on training-set completeness and the active-learning protocol.
Failure to reduce the thermodynamic-integration mismatch by at least 50% relative to the TOR-TILD EAM reference is proposed as the falsification criterion.

contradictions.description: The predicted target is below 5%, whereas the falsification rule nominally requires only a 50% reduction from a stated 15% baseline, corresponding to 7.5%. The rule's parenthetical further says failure means remaining above approximately 10–15%, which is not equivalent to failing a 50% reduction and leaves outcomes around 8–10% ambiguously classified.
